statement.text:
Let G be a finite non-abelian group, and Z(G) its centre. One can associate a
graph ΓG with G as follows: take G\Z(G) as vertices of ΓG and join two vertices x
and y if xy ̸= yx. Let H be a finite non-abelian group such that ΓG ∼= ΓH .
    b) If H is nilpotent, is it true that G is nilpotent?
   Comment of 2009: This is true if |H| = |G| (A. Abdollahi, S. Akbari,
H. R. Maimani, J. Algebra, 298 (2006), 468–492).
   Comments of 2023: This is true if |Z(H)| ⩾ |Z(G)| (H. Shahverdi, J. Algebra,
642 (2024), 60–64), using the earlier result under the additional assumption that
the centralizer of every non-central element in H is abelian (V. Grazian, C. Monetta,
J. Algebra, 633 (2023), 389–402).
    c) If H is solvable, is it true that G is solvable?
                                                A. Abdollahi, S. Akbari, H. R. Maimani
